Transport layer routing mechanism \\nThe guiding price of a path is calculated based on the carrier quote. \\nAccording to different characteristics, paths are classified into distance \\nvector master path and link-state branch paths, corresponding to inter- \\nautonomous area links and intra-autonomous area links, respectively. \\nIn this study, we developed the CPI routing mechanism based on the \\nfollowing assumptions: (1) The PI containers flowing in the CPI logistics \\nnetwork are all standard boxes with the same weight, volume, and type, \\n(2) Distance vector links can provide sufficient capacity, while link-state \\npaths have limited capacity, (3) Each link is associated with a carrier \\nquote. Links covering the distance vector master path are charged based \\non transport distance, while links covering the link state branch path are \\ncharged based on the number of PI containers to be transported. (4) The \\ncarrier is only allowed to quote once in a short period and the quote \\nremains unchanged for the duration of the logistics process. \\nThe CPI routing mechanism adopted in the CPI transport layer is \\npresented in Fig. 4. At the beginning, the demand quantity and desti-\\nnation of the PI container should be clarified. Then, the status of each \\npath that connects the current node is checked according to the routing \\ntable. If the path status is healthy, it can be quoted by carriers to \\ngenerate links. Correspondingly, road repairs, road closure and the \\nexhaustion of link capacity would cause the path to be identified as \\nunhealthy, and the overhead of unhealthy paths will be set to an infinite \\nvalue to avoid being selected for routing. The routing table is updated in \\nreal time, showing the optimal next-hop path that reaches the destina -\\ntion with the least overhead for the current node at that time. If the next \\nhop is the destination, the routes, routing distance and total overhead \\ncan be output. Otherwise, the current node will be replaced by the next \\nhop, and the process will be re-executed until the PI container reaches its \\ndestination. \\nThe charging methods are various according to different types of \\npaths. Since the market for master paths is saturated, multiple carriers \\ncan provide transport service for a path and the capacity of the distance \\nvector path is sufficient. Neither carriers nor other logistics participants \\ncan affect the market price of links for distance vector paths by \\nmonopolizing the capacity. The market price only depends on the supply \\nand demand. The overhead of a distance vector path mainly depends on \\nthe transport distance. Carriers use unit distance quotes for distance \\nvector paths and compete to provide transport service. Therefore, ac-\\ncording to the DVMP routing mechanism, the unit distance quotes from \\nall participating carriers should first be obtained. Then, the quotes are \\nmultiplied by the distance and the number of PI containers to get the \\ngradient price for the path. The link with the smallest gradient price will \\nbe selected as the optimal link, and the gradient price for the corre -\\nsponding link as the path overhead will be added to the total overhead. \\nThe capacity provided by carriers is generally limited due to the \\nmode of transport in branch paths. They usually give a ladder price \\nbased on the quantity of PI containers. For the reason of limited re-\\nsources, the unit price gets higher as the number of PI containers in-\\ncreases. Therefore, according to the LSBP routing mechanism, the ladder \\nprice quotes from all participating carriers should first be obtained. \\nThen, the guiding prices corresponding to the quantity of PI containers \\nare calculated based on the gradient price. The carrier that provides the \\nlink with the smallest gradient price will be first selected to provide \\ntransport service. However, if too many PI containers are shipped on the \\nsame path, they may be shared by more than one carrier. For instance, a \\ncarrier provides a link with a capacity of 30 units for a unit price of 25, \\nbut from the 31st unit, which is the second link provided by the carrier, \\nthe unit price becomes 30. Another carrier ’s first link provides 20 units \\nof capacity at a unit price of 28, but the unit price for its second link \\nbecomes 32. If a total of 40 units of PI containers are to be shipped to the \\nsame destination, the two carriers will be selected to transport together, \\nand the path overhead should be the sum of the guiding prices of the two \\nlinks. At the link layer, a LEAF \\nmethod is adopted to divide the region into several autonomous areas \\nand to establish connections between them by electing core autonomous \\nareas and regional link centers. The DVMP routing \\nmechanism and LSBP routing mechanism are proposed based on the \\ndistance vector characteristics and the path state characteristics of the \\npath, respectively. Moreover, the \\nLEAF method improves network response efficiency and disaster \\ntolerance through a weighted distance function and core autono -\\nmous area election.
